solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Knave in charge of wobbly kago with judge on board making anything but smooth progress

indicators.note: something wobbly is unsteady and shifting, so the letters that follow move about
a passenger on board is inside the vessel, so one piece is placed within the other

blocks.note: J is the card abbreviation for jack, the knave
standard abbreviation for in charge
a Japanese palanquin, taken as written before rearranging
J is the abbreviation for judge

explanation.surface: A rogue in charge of a shaky Japanese litter, with a judge aboard, makes for a bumpy ride.
explanation.walkthrough: A kago is a Japanese palanquin, a covered litter carried on poles. Knave and judge both abbreviate to J, so the answer has two.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambers gives jickajog as a jolting, jerky motion, the opposite of a smooth advance.

clue.text: Eye sweet: fool?

blocks.note: a private eye is a detective, and jack is slang for a detective
a pudding is a sweet course

explanation.surface: Eye, sweet, fool: a list of things, with fool also a fruit dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: A fool is also a creamy fruit pudding, so 'sweet: fool?' looks like a dessert definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A jack-pudding is a buffoon or clown, an old word for a fool or merry-andrew.

clue.text: Like a symbol I see on either side of leg

indicators.note: something on either side of a word flanks it, enclosing it

blocks.note: I plus the letter C, which sounds like see
leg side and on side are the same half of a cricket field
used again for the other side

explanation.surface: Someone spots a symbol on both sides of a leg, perhaps a tattoo.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the leg side is also called the on side, so leg gives ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Iconic means of or like an icon, an image standing for something.

clue.text: Mites one removed from above and around fruit trees

indicators.note: in a down entry the top is the start, so a letter is taken off the front

blocks.note: Acari is the scientific name for mites and ticks
ca is the abbreviation of circa, around

explanation.surface: Mites are cleared from above and around some fruit trees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' is A, the first letter of ACARI, removed from the top.
explanation.definitionFit: Carica is the genus of papaya trees, which bear fruit.

clue.text: Some cats raking up limestone tract

indicators.note: some of the words means only a portion of their letters
in a down entry, up means reading from the bottom to the top

blocks.note: the letters spanning the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: Cats scratching at a stretch of limestone country.
explanation.definitionFit: Karst is limestone landscape full of fissures, sinkholes and caves, named after a region in Slovenia.

clue.text: Traitor while following Trump (not one Democrat)?

indicators.note: not one means a single copy is left out

blocks.note: Judd Trump is an English snooker champion
D for Democrat, the letter removed
as means while

explanation.surface: A political jibe calling a Trump follower a traitor, minus a Democrat.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface points at Donald Trump, but this Trump is snooker player Judd Trump, whose first name loses one D.
explanation.definitionFit: Judas Iscariot betrayed Jesus, and his name is used for any betrayer.

clue.text: Tasteless adornment, not new

indicators.note: not means without, so a letter is removed

blocks.note: a garnish adorns a dish
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A judgement that some old decoration is in poor taste.
explanation.definitionFit: Garish means showy and lurid, lacking good taste in colour or display.

clue.text: Baby's mum wiping bottom – not something one could get out of!

definitions.text: not something one could get out of!

indicators.note: wiping something away removes it, so letters are taken out here

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
British slang for the backside; these three letters are the ones wiped out

explanation.surface: A parent cleaning a baby's bottom, with a wry aside about a situation there is no escape from.
explanation.walkthrough: The B, U and M removed are scattered: the first B, the U and the final M of BABYSMUM, leaving ABYSM. 'Bum' is British slang for bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: An abysm is an abyss, a bottomless pit that nobody could climb out of.

clue.text: Rat run, a pest, going round outskirts of Yeovil

indicators.note: going round something surrounds it
outskirts are the edges, so only the outer letters count

blocks.note: a bane is a pest or nuisance
Yeovil is a Somerset town; its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A rat scuttling round the edge of a Somerset town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rat run' looks like the rodent, but a rat run is a minor road drivers use to dodge traffic.
explanation.definitionFit: A bylane is a side lane, the sort of back road that serves as a shortcut.

clue.text: Tent for travellers, not our type principally?

indicators.note: principally means at the head, so just the first letter

blocks.note: if it is not ours, it is yours
its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone sniffs that a travellers' tent is not really their sort of thing.
explanation.definitionFit: A yourt, usually yurt, is the round felt tent of Central Asian nomads.

clue.text: Fillet in quarters Scots served up

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word reads from bottom to top

blocks.note: airts is Scots for the quarters or directions of the compass

explanation.surface: A cut of fish served to Scots in quarters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fillet' suggests a cut of meat or fish; here it is the architectural sense.
explanation.definitionFit: In architecture a stria is a fillet, the narrow flat band between the flutes of a column.

clue.text: See rims messed up round melon being divided into segments

indicators.note: messed up means put in disarray, so letters are rearranged
going round something encloses it

blocks.note: taken as written before rearranging
Ogen is a variety of small sweet melon

explanation.surface: A messy plate of melon, its rims ragged, cut into pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: Segmenting a melon fits the surface neatly; the definition is biological.
explanation.definitionFit: Merogenesis is the formation of body segments in animals such as worms, segmentation in biology.

clue.text: Higher organism turning 'tail' pursued by a peasant farmer with energy

indicators.note: turning round sends the word back the other way

blocks.note: cue is an old spelling of queue, a pigtail or tail
taken as written
a ryot is an Indian peasant farmer
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A tale of a peasant farmer chasing something with vigour, oddly involving a tail.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks around 'tail' flag that it stands for another word: CUE, the pigtail sense of queue.
explanation.definitionFit: A eucaryote is an organism whose cells have a nucleus, as opposed to the simpler bacteria.

clue.text: Like barley sugar, say, or chocolate, one of Easter's pair replacing egg?

indicators.note: replacing means one letter takes the place of another
barley sugar is twisted, so the letters are twisted out of order

blocks.note: taken as written
Easter has two Es; one of them
an egg is O-shaped; the letter that is swapped out

explanation.surface: Easter treats: twisted barley sugar or chocolate eggs.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition does double duty as the anagram signal: barley sugar is twisted, and so is the chocolate once an E has replaced an O. Commenters on the blog debated whether this is fair.
explanation.definitionFit: Cochleate means spirally twisted like a snail shell, the shape of barley-sugar sticks.

clue.text: Wherein political gossip circulates, 'ideous in endless run

indicators.note: without an end, so the final letter is dropped
one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: a corso is an Italian street or course, a run
the dropped aitch of 'ideous shows horrid without its H

explanation.surface: A Cockney complaint that political gossip is hideous, in a never-ending stream.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'ideous shows a dropped H, so its synonym must drop its H too. A corso is an Italian avenue or course, hence run.
explanation.definitionFit: The corridors of power are where politicians whisper and rumours spread, an idiom for behind-the-scenes politics.

clue.text: Jewish speciality, hot, to collapse? Reverse of this

indicators.note: the clue tells us the answer is the preceding wordplay read backwards

blocks.note: H is the tap abbreviation for hot
to sink is to collapse or subside

explanation.surface: A hot Jewish dish that might collapse, with a teasing instruction to turn things around.
explanation.definitionFit: A knish is a baked or fried dumpling of dough filled with potato, a classic Ashkenazi food.

clue.text: Super character I found in Vergil

indicators.note: something found in another sits inside it

blocks.note: taken as written
the poet's full name was Publius Vergilius Maro

explanation.surface: A reader claims to have found a great character in Virgil's poetry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Super' looks like praise for the character; it is the Super of the video game title.
explanation.definitionFit: Mario is the plumber hero of Nintendo's Super Mario games, a game character.

clue.text: Old Scottish ship capsized – 100 on it overturned inside

indicators.note: a capsized vessel is thrown upside down, so its letters are disordered
turned over, so the short word runs backwards
the following pieces go within the other

blocks.note: taken as written before rearranging
C is the Roman numeral for 100
taken as written

explanation.surface: An old Scottish ship has overturned with a hundred aboard.
explanation.walkthrough: SHIP becomes PISH, and C followed by the backwards IT goes into the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: The Picts were an ancient people of northern Scotland, so Pictish describes something early Scottish.

clue.text: Cape for woman or unaccompanied man, might one conclude?

blocks.note: first meaning: a knitted cape worn by women, named after a singer
second, cryptic meaning: read the answer as an instruction, S placed on TAG, and it gives STAG, a man without a partner

explanation.walkthrough: The second half reverses the usual direction: the answer split as S ON TAG is a recipe for STAG, and a stag party or stag is a man on his own.
explanation.definitionFit: A sontag is a crocheted or knitted cape with long ends crossed over the chest, a period women's garment.

clue.text: Skipper briefly bagging duck, but it's worth 40 points

indicators.note: bagging something puts it inside a bag, so one piece encloses another

blocks.note: the short form of captain, the skipper
a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, O

explanation.surface: A cricket captain out for a duck, yet somehow still scoring 40.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket picture makes 40 points look like runs; the definition is from the card game piquet.
explanation.definitionFit: In piquet, capot is winning every trick of a hand, which earns a bonus of forty points.

clue.text: Being free of taint, showing compassion about what's at centre of hurt

indicators.note: about means surrounding something
the centre is the middle, so only the middle letters are kept

blocks.note: pity is compassion
its two middle letters

explanation.surface: A pure soul shows compassion for whatever lies at the heart of a hurt.
explanation.definitionFit: Purity is the state of being unpolluted, without contamination or moral stain.

clue.text: Very old coat? Half of it covers more than half of terrier

indicators.note: half of a two-letter word is a single letter
more than half means the word is cut short but keeps most of itself

blocks.note: its second letter
an Aberdeen terrier is a Scottish terrier

explanation.surface: A dog's very old coat, half covered by something.
explanation.walkthrough: The Aberdeen terrier is another name for the Scottish terrier. 'covers' means the first piece sits on top in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Taberd is an obsolete spelling of tabard, a short tunic worn over armour or by heralds.

clue.text: Cutters in sound? They may be looking out for shoals

definitions.text: They may be looking out for shoals

indicators.note: in sound means as heard, so the spelling follows the pronunciation of another word

blocks.note: hewers are those who cut wood or stone

explanation.surface: Woodcutters in a sound, a stretch of water, keeping a watch for shallows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' and 'shoals' both suggest the sea, as do the hazards of shallows; the shoals are of fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A huer was a lookout on Cornish cliffs who shouted to boats when shoals of pilchards appeared.

clue.text: I'm opening sprinkler with lots of little holes

indicators.note: something opening another splits it apart and sits inside

blocks.note: taken as written
a rose is the perforated nozzle of a watering can

explanation.surface: A gardener opens a sprinkler riddled with holes.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage the rose is the perforated spray head on a watering can.
explanation.definitionFit: Rimose means full of chinks or cracks, as of bark, close to being riddled with small openings.

clue.text: Regular helpings of beer is imbibed by drunk once provided

indicators.note: regular helpings means taking letters at even intervals
something imbibed is swallowed and so ends up inside

blocks.note: a sot is a drunkard
the first, third and fifth letters

explanation.surface: A drunk who once swigged regular helpings of beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'once' marks the definition as archaic.
explanation.definitionFit: Sobeit is an old conjunction meaning on condition that, from so be it.

clue.text: In retrospect rue being taken in by flyer for poisonous apple?

indicators.note: looking back in retrospect sends the whole result backwards
taken in means enclosed by something else

blocks.note: a flyer is a leaflet advertisement, an ad
Ruta is the genus name of the herb rue

explanation.surface: Someone regrets being fooled by a leaflet about a dangerous fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rue' reads as regret, but it is the plant whose Latin name supplies the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Datura includes the thorn apple, a toxic plant, hence the question mark on this apple.

clue.text: Tool used in erection of fireguard

indicators.note: used in means the letters are taken from within the following word
erecting raises something up, so in a down entry it reads upwards

blocks.note: the letters in the middle of the word

explanation.surface: A tool used to put up a fireguard.
explanation.definitionFit: An auger is a boring tool for making holes in wood or the ground.

clue.text: This sec last? It's confused with claret maybe

indicators.note: confused letters are mixed together out of order
this points to the answer itself, which joined with another word gives the jumble, so that word is taken away

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written; maybe just hedges the surface
taken as written; the part removed

explanation.surface: A wine buff asks whether this dry wine comes last and is mistaken for claret.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: the answer plus LAST is a jumble of IT'S CLARET, so removing LAST leaves the answer. 'sec' looks like dry wine but means a second.
explanation.definitionFit: A trice is an instant, and sec is short for second, also a brief moment.

clue.text: Being busy, no time to make room for love and suchlike

indicators.note: busy letters are bustling about, so they rearrange
making room for something means letting it in among the others

blocks.note: taken as written before rearranging
love is zero in tennis, O

explanation.surface: Too busy to make time for love and the like.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition shares 'love' with the wordplay: love is both the O and one of the feelings defined.
explanation.definitionFit: Love is a feeling, so love and similar feelings are emotions.

clue.text: Tangle of brushwood ideal for conifer

blocks.note: a mat is a tangled mass, as of twigs or hair
A1 means first-rate, ideal, written with I for 1

explanation.surface: A thicket of brushwood would be just right for a conifer.
explanation.definitionFit: The matai is a New Zealand coniferous tree, also called black pine.

clue.text: What scavenger's retrieved – one left little amount

blocks.note: a tot is anything salvaged from rubbish, the haul of a totter
a means one
L, the abbreviation, a little form of left

explanation.surface: A scavenger's haul leaves only a small amount behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'little' signals that left is shortened to its abbreviation; a totter is a rag-and-bone scavenger.
explanation.definitionFit: A total is a whole sum or quantity, an amount reached by adding up.

clue.text: Just like mater, accepting recipe for cereal

indicators.note: accepting something takes it in, so a letter goes inside

blocks.note: dura mater is the tough membrane round the brain, so dura goes with mater
R is the abbreviation for recipe, from Latin, on prescriptions

explanation.surface: Someone takes a recipe just as mother did.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mater' looks like the schoolboy's word for mother; it is the anatomical term.
explanation.definitionFit: Durra is a variety of sorghum grown as a grain crop in Africa and Asia.

clue.text: What's enjoyed in Kenyan tavern? British ale, without hesitation

indicators.note: without means lacking, so a part is taken away

blocks.note: Pom is Australian slang for a Briton
ale is a kind of beer
er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A drinker in a Kenyan bar enjoys British ale without pause.
explanation.definitionFit: Pombe is a traditional fermented millet or banana beer of East and Central Africa.

clue.text: Indulged girls fed with old English trotters

indicators.note: being fed with something takes it inside

blocks.note: to pet is to indulge or pamper
tit is old slang for a girl
O is a standard abbreviation for old
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: Spoilt girls are fed pig's feet, old English fare.
explanation.definitionFit: Pettitoes are pigs' feet cooked as food, which is what trotters means on a menu.

clue.text: Sweet client I'll leave dancing round floor

indicators.note: leaving means departing, so a letter goes
dancing letters move about into a new order
going round something encloses it

blocks.note: taken as written
read as I will, so I is the letter that departs
the floor area of a room

explanation.surface: A sweet-talking client announces they will leave the dance floor.
explanation.walkthrough: Read I'll as 'I will': the instruction is that the letter I will leave, a trick that hides the indicator inside a contraction.
explanation.definitionFit: Nectareal means like nectar, that is sweet-tasting, a rare poetic adjective.

clue.text: Regimental horses to feed by the sound of it

indicators.note: the pronunciation of a word is what counts here, not its spelling

blocks.note: to graze is to feed on grass

explanation.surface: Cavalry horses need to feed, it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal Scots Greys were a British cavalry regiment mounted on grey horses.
explanation.definitionFit: Greys are grey horses, and the regiment named after its mounts took the same name.

clue.text: Drops backward booby, say – why don't we?

indicators.note: backward means running the opposite way

blocks.note: a booby is a seabird, an example of a bird
let's is the suggestion why don't we

explanation.surface: A dim-witted idiot drops back, and someone suggests a plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'booby' looks like a fool, but 'say' marks it as an example: the gannet-like seabird.
explanation.definitionFit: Driblets are small drops of liquid, tiny drips or quantities.
